_: ONE table for the design lifecycle's state rule (docs/hub/design.md, "State -- derived, never stored"), read by both readers of it: Scripts/Read-DesignTree.ps1 Resolve-P20DesignState (tkTestToolkit -Design) and agent/ado/design.py design_state() (Tests/test_design.py). The unit is the design: one id, a note and at most one spec. `note` and `spec` say where each file is -- live (design/ or spec/), archive (design/archive/ or spec/archive/), or null for none -- and noteLines / specLines are footer lines the file carries. expected is the state, the outcome a note archived without a spec may carry (null otherwise), whether the two files disagree about where the design is (mismatch -- the spec's folder wins and the row says so), the Closed date, a fact about a design that has REACHED an archive state: the spec's for Complete, the note's for Archived, '' for Design and Spec (a note archived before its spec is still a Spec), and ready, a fact about a LIVE design someone has marked finished (docs/hub/design.md, "Marking a live design finished"): a Design with no spec whose note's first Outcome line says exactly shipped (case ignored, nothing after it), or a Spec whose live spec carries a non-empty `> Docs:` line and neither file's Outcome word is dropped. If the two halves ever disagree about a row, one of them is wrong.

rows.name: a note alone
a note with its spec beside it
both archived: built, and documented
a note archived alone, nothing said of it
the spec archived, the note left behind in design/
the note archived before its spec
a spec standing without a note
an archived spec standing without a note
an idea that never made it
a deck design that shipped as written
a live note marked shipped is ready: the outcome stays a fact of an archived note, so it reads none, and the line is read as ready instead
a Complete design needs no outcome: its spec was built, and a stray line is not read
a spec dropped: both archived, the spec carries the dropped outcome, so it reads Archived, not Complete
an outcome word outside the contract's two reads as none
a live note marked shipped in its footer, beside its Created line, is ready to archive
the outcome word is compared ignoring case: SHIPPED is ready
a live note marked dropped is not ready: dropping a design needs its reason, so the word is never a trigger
shipped with a date after it is no outcome word, so the note is not ready
a note marked shipped whose spec is live is not ready: the spec is what is waiting
a live spec with a Docs line, beside its live note, is ready to complete
a live spec with a Docs line and no note is ready to complete
a live spec with a Docs line whose note says dropped is not ready: the two marks conflict
a live spec with a Docs line that itself says dropped is not ready
a live spec with a Docs line, its note already archived, is ready and still says the two disagree
a Complete pair carrying both lines is done, not ready
a live note marked shipped whose spec is archived is Complete and a mismatch, not ready
